doc: Declarative policy for scripts/check-r75.js. Every banned literal lives here as DATA, never assembled in executable source, so the checker's own source cannot evade its own scan (AGENT_RULES R109 exception-class discipline). This file is .json and therefore outside scan.includeExtensions, so the policy is not self-matched.

scan.note: Application AND test sources are in scope, top-level and nested, including co-located *.spec.* / *.test.* files: R131 records that reading R75 as src-only was a misreading. There is no spec/test exclusion. Declaration files, minified bundles, vendored and generated trees are the only narrow exclusions. Fixture DATA is out of scope solely because .json is not an executable extension; executable tests are always scanned.

patternTokens.name: as any
patternTokens.why: Word-bounded so 'has anything' cannot false-positive and multi-space casts cannot evade; matches the pre-existing lefthook regex semantics.

patternTokens.name: empty-catch
patternTokens.why: One detector for every spelling of the swallowed-error catch (50-failures #36): zero-arg and parametrized, with or without spaces, typed or async. The previous split of three no-space literals plus a parametrized regex matched NEITHER '.catch(() => null)' NOR '.catch(() => {})' — the exact forms Prettier produces — so the canonical R75 literals were undetectable in formatted source.

suppressions.why: R75 permits '@ts-expect-error <reason>' with a single-line non-empty reason. No issue-number requirement exists in canon and none is invented here. The exception discounts ONLY that directive occurrence; every other banned token on the same line is still counted.
